rationale: Yes: when a developer publishes an update, the request shows Pending update, and users keep the previous version until you approve it with Update in store.
No: the request workflow supports only Microsoft-built agents. Users cannot request third-party agents such as Ski Rental Partner through it, and admins cannot approve them there.
Yes: the audience selected in the publishing wizard is the set of users who can install the agent, so MountainOps members alone can install Trail Guide.

stem:
Graphic Design Institute has an agent named Agent1 that is available in the agent registry. Every member of the design team must have Agent1 ready to use without installing it themselves.

Which action should you select in the agent details pane?
choices: Install
Pin for users
Unblock
Publish to store
explanation: Install deploys an agent for selected users or the whole organization so users do not have to install it. Availability decides who may install it, pinning only makes it more visible, and blocking stops all use.
rationale: Correct: Install deploys the agent to the users or groups you select, after you review and consent to its permissions, so it is ready without manual installation.
Incorrect: pinning works only for agents that are already deployed and only changes where the agent appears. Use it after installation to make the agent prominent.
Incorrect: Unblock restores an agent that was blocked. Agent1 is available, not blocked, so unblocking changes nothing. Use it to reverse a block decision.
Incorrect: Publish to store approves an agent request so users can install it themselves. It does not preinstall the agent. Use it for submitted agents.

stem:
Margie's Travel must make the Researcher agent unavailable to all users while a compliance review is in progress. In the agent details of Researcher, the Edit users panel is disabled.

What should you do?
choices: Block the agent for the entire tenant
Uninstall the agent for all users
Remove the agent from Manage pinned agents
Clear the Microsoft option in Agent and plugin access
explanation: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled, so availability cannot be scoped per user. Learn directs admins to block the agent for the entire tenant to manage its availability.
rationale: Correct: Learn states that for Researcher and Analyst you manage availability by blocking the agent for the entire tenant with the Block action.
Incorrect: uninstalling removes an installed agent but users could install it again, so it does not make Researcher unavailable during the review. Use it to remove a deployment.
Incorrect: unpinning only removes Researcher from the pinned list. Users can still find and use it. Use pinning to change visibility, not availability.

Incorrect: clearing the Microsoft option stops users from installing every agent and plugin built by Microsoft, not only Researcher, so it is far broader than the compliance review needs. Use it to block a whole publisher category.

stem:
Lucerne Publishing publishes an agent named Agent2. Only members of the Analysts group may discover and install Agent2 themselves. Members of the Executives group, who are not analysts, must have Agent2 preinstalled.

How should you configure the Users tab of Agent2?
choices: Available to: Analysts; Installed to: Executives
Available to: All users; Installed to: Executives
Available to: Analysts and Executives; Installed to: Entire organization
Available to: No users; Installed to: Executives
explanation: Availability (who can discover and install) and installation (who has the agent preinstalled) are independent. An install reaches targeted users even when they are outside the availability audience, which lets you preinstall for one group and offer to another.
rationale: Correct: Available to Analysts limits self-service install to analysts, and Installed to Executives preinstalls the agent for executives even though they are not in the availability audience.
Incorrect: All users lets everyone discover and install Agent2, which breaks only analysts may install it. Use it for agents meant for the whole company.
Incorrect: installing to the entire organization installs the agent for everyone regardless of availability, which goes far beyond the executives. Use it for company-wide agents.
Incorrect: No users stops analysts from installing the agent themselves. Use it when an agent should only reach users through admin installation.

stem:
A. Datum Corporation blocks an agent that a user created in SharePoint. A day later, users can no longer use the agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat but still use it in the SharePoint site where it was created.

What should you tell the help desk?
choices: Blocking a SharePoint agent affects only its availability in Copilot Chat
Blocking applies only after you also uninstall the agent for all users
Blocking affects only users who did not install the agent before the block
Blocking a SharePoint agent requires the Azure AI Owner role to take effect
explanation: Blocking an Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agent affects Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams. Blocking an agent created with SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry affects only its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
rationale: Correct: Learn states that blocking an agent created with SharePoint only impacts its availability in Copilot Chat, which matches what users see.
Incorrect: Block works on its own; uninstalling is a separate action that removes a deployment. Use Uninstall when an installed agent should be removed but stay allowed.
Incorrect: a block also removes the agent from members who already installed it. The behavior in the stem comes from the agent type, not from install state.
Incorrect: Azure AI Owner is needed to start or stop the Azure infrastructure of Foundry agents, not to block agents. Block needs only an agent admin role.

stem:
Fourth Coffee wants to pin an HR agent for all users in Microsoft 365 Copilot. The agent is published and available to all users, but no one has it installed. When you try to pin it, a banner asks you to take another action first.

What should you do first?
choices: Install the agent for the users
Unblock the agent
Move the agent up in the pinned list
Add a tag to the agent
explanation: Administrators can pin up to three deployed agents for all users or for groups. Only deployed agents can be pinned, blocked agents must be unblocked first, and pinned agents can take up to six hours to appear.
rationale: Correct: you can pin only deployed agents, and the banner asks you to deploy first, so installing the HR agent for the users comes before pinning.
Incorrect: unblocking is required only when the agent is blocked. The HR agent is available, so the block banner would not appear. Unblock first for blocked agents.
Incorrect: ranking with Move up and Move down applies to agents already in the pinned list. The HR agent cannot be added yet.
Incorrect: tags organize and filter agents in the registry but do not affect pinning. Use tags to group agents by team or function.

stem:
Tailspin Toys built a custom agent in Microsoft Copilot Studio. The developer will not submit it for approval. You must add the agent to the Microsoft 365 admin center so that only the TestGroup group can install it, with the default policy template.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: In Copilot Studio, go to Channels > Teams and Microsoft Copilot > Availability options, and select Download .zip.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > All agents > Add agent, choose the ZIP file, and select Next.
Verify the agent's name, icon and host products, and under Publish select TestGroup.
Apply the default policy template, and select Next.
Review the agent permissions, select Next, and then select Finish deployment.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Tools > Registry, and select Upload.
On the Requests tab, select the agent, and then select Publish to store.
explanation: The registry can take a custom agent as a ZIP package that contains manifests, icons and embedded knowledge. You download the ZIP from Copilot Studio or Agent Builder, upload it with Add agent, choose the publish (and optional deploy) audience, apply a template and finish.
rationale: Step 1: Add agent needs a ZIP package, which you download from the Copilot Studio channel availability options.
Step 2: Add agent in the agent registry uploads and validates the ZIP file.
Step 3: after validation you verify the agent details, and the Publish selection defines who can install the agent, here TestGroup.
Step 4: the next page applies an existing, custom or default policy template; the default template meets the requirement.
Step 5: the permissions review and Finish deployment complete the upload.
Incorrect: Upload in the Tools registry takes manifest files for plugins and skills, not agent ZIP packages. Use it to add a plugin or skill.
Incorrect: the Requests tab only lists agents that were submitted for approval. The developer will not submit this agent, so no request exists.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank has Microsoft Agent 365 licenses. You must block an agent package in the registry by using Microsoft Graph PowerShell and the least privileged permission.

How should you complete the script? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

```powershell
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes '[[1]]'
$packageId = 'P_19ae1zz1-56bc-505a-3d42-156df75a4xxy'
Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method [[2]] -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/$packageId/[[3]]"
```
explanation: The Package Management API blocks an agent with POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block (beta), which needs the delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission and returns 204 No Content. Unblock and reassign are sibling POST actions.

why: Correct: CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All is the least privileged delegated permission for the block action.
Incorrect: CopilotPackages.Read.All allows listing and reading packages only; the block call would be denied.
Incorrect: AppCatalog.ReadWrite.All manages the Teams app catalog and does not authorize the Agent 365 package API.
Correct: block is an action, invoked with POST and no request body.
Incorrect: PATCH updates package metadata on the package itself, not the block action.
Incorrect: DELETE is not how the API blocks a package. Deleting an agent is a separate admin action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Correct: the block action prevents usage of the package across the organization.
Incorrect: unblock reverses an earlier block and allows usage of the package again, which is the opposite of the goal.
Incorrect: reassign changes the owner of the package, for example when an employee leaves.

stem:
Refer to the case study. You need to meet the business requirements for Lift Status.

Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: On the Users tab of Lift Status, set Available to MountainOps.
On the Users tab of Lift Status, set Installed to LiftOperators.
In Manage pinned agents, pin Lift Status for LiftOperators.
On the Users tab of Lift Status, set Installed to Entire organization.
Upload the Lift Status ZIP file again by using Add agent.
Set User access to Specific users or groups, and select LiftOperators.
explanation: Availability, installation and pinning are separate controls. Available to decides who can install, Installed to preinstalls the agent, and pinning (up to three agents, deployed agents only) makes it prominent in Microsoft 365 Copilot for selected users.
rationale: Correct: Available to MountainOps lets every mountain operations member install Lift Status, as the case requires.
Correct: Installed to LiftOperators preinstalls the agent for lift operators so they need no action, and it makes the agent deployed so it can be pinned.
Correct: admins can pin deployed agents for specific groups, so pinning Lift Status for LiftOperators makes it appear pinned in Copilot.
Incorrect: installing to the entire organization preinstalls Lift Status for every employee, including seasonal staff, which goes beyond the lift operators. Use it for company-wide agents.

Incorrect: Lift Status is already published to the organization, so uploading its ZIP again would add a second entry without meeting any requirement. Use Add agent for agents that are not in the registry.
Incorrect: User access is tenant-wide; limiting it to LiftOperators would stop the other pilot participants from using any agent.

stem:
At Proseware, Inc., a developer registered a remote MCP server with Microsoft Agent 365. You must review the server name, the requester and the declared tools before the server becomes available in the organizational registry.

Which location should you use?
choices: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Requests
Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Requests
Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Gateways
Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Admin consent requests
explanation: Tools such as MCP servers, plugins, skills and connectors are governed on the Tools page of the Microsoft 365 admin center. A registered MCP server appears on its Requests (preview) tab, where an admin approves or rejects it and then consents to its Entra permissions.
rationale: Correct: the Requests (preview) tab under Agents > Tools lists MCP server registration requests with server name, publisher, requester, date and declared tools.
Incorrect: the Requests tab under All agents holds agent submissions, updates and activations, not tool registrations. Use it to publish agents.
Incorrect: Gateways connects Azure AI Gateway or LiteLLM so that their MCP servers are discovered. Individual registrations are not reviewed there.
Incorrect: admin consent requests are for apps that users ask to consent to. Consent for an MCP server is granted after you approve it on the Tools page.

stem:
Bellows College uses an MCP server registered on Agent 365 that supports tool discovery. It exposes read tools and a tool named delete_record. Agents must keep using the read tools but must never call delete_record.

What should you do in Agents > Tools?
choices: On the Tools tab of the server, disable delete_record, and save
Block the MCP server in the Tools registry
Block the plugins that use the MCP server
Uninstall the MCP server from the Tools registry
explanation: Blocking an MCP server disables every tool it exposes. Tool-level granular control lets you turn off individual tools on supported servers, such as write or delete tools, while lower-risk tools stay enabled. The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the setting at runtime. Tool-level control is rolling out only for specific server types; support for bring-your-own MCP servers is planned, so use a server-level block for those.
rationale: Correct: the Tools tab lists each tool with an Enabled or Disabled toggle, so disabling delete_record and saving blocks only that tool, enforced at runtime by the Tooling Gateway.
Incorrect: blocking the server disables all the tools it exposes, including the read tools that agents still need. Use it when the whole server must be stopped.
Incorrect: blocking plugins stops the plugins and their dependent agents, while the server and delete_record stay available to other clients. Use it to stop a specific plugin package.
Incorrect: uninstall applies to plugins and skills and would remove all capabilities, not only delete_record. Use tool-level control for a single risky tool.

stem:
Relecloud developers register remote MCP servers with Agent 365. You must assign a role to an administrator who reviews these requests on the Tools page and grants the required tenant-wide consent. You must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which role should you assign?
choices: AI Administrator
Global Administrator
Cloud Application Administrator
AI Reader
explanation: Approving MCP server requests needs two things: access to the Tools page in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the ability to grant tenant-wide consent. Learn names AI Administrator and Global Administrator as the roles that meet both, and AI Administrator is the narrower one.
rationale: Correct: AI Administrator can access the Tools page and grant tenant-wide consent, and it is less privileged than Global Administrator.
Incorrect: Global Administrator meets both requirements but is a highly privileged role. Use it only when no narrower role works, such as connecting a gateway.
Incorrect: Cloud Application Administrator can grant consent to many apps, but it is not one of the roles that Learn lists for reviewing MCP requests on the Tools page.
Incorrect: AI Reader gives read-only visibility of agents and cannot approve requests or grant consent. Use it for auditors.

stem:
Contoso, Ltd. registered its MCP servers in Azure API Management with the AI Gateway tier. An administrator who has the AI Administrator role cannot connect the gateway in Agents > Settings > Gateways in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What should you do?
choices: Have a Global Administrator turn on the Microsoft Azure toggle and consent
Assign the Azure AI Owner role to the administrator and retry
Approve each MCP server of the gateway on the Tools Requests tab
Register each MCP server again by using the Agent 365 CLI
explanation: Connecting Azure AI Gateway to Agent 365 requires the Global Administrator role; AI Administrator does not support it. Consent is given once per tenant for all MCP servers in the gateway, and the servers are then discovered on the Tools page.
rationale: Correct: Learn requires the Global Administrator role to connect Azure AI Gateway. The Global Administrator turns on the Microsoft Azure toggle and accepts the permissions once for the tenant.
Incorrect: Azure AI Owner is needed to start or stop the infrastructure of Foundry agents, not to connect a gateway in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Incorrect: gateway servers are discovered automatically after the connection, and consent covers all of them, so no per-server request exists. Use the Requests tab for BYO registrations.
Incorrect: the CLI registers bring-your-own MCP servers with Agent 365. The gateway servers are already registered in API Management and only need the connection.

stem:
Litware, Inc. has an MCP server named MCP1. Two plugins use MCP1: Plugin1, which your organization uploaded, and Plugin2, which comes from the Microsoft 365 Store.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
choices: If you block MCP1, the plugins that depend on MCP1 and its linked connectors are also blocked.
If you block Plugin1, MCP1 becomes unavailable to Plugin2.
You can delete Plugin2 from the Tools registry.
explanation: Blocking flows downward from a server: blocking an MCP server also blocks dependent plugins and linked connectors. Blocking a plugin affects that plugin and its agents only. Delete applies only to plugins and skills that were uploaded to the tenant.
rationale: Yes: Learn states that blocking an MCP server also blocks dependent plugins and linked connectors, so both Plugin1 and Plugin2 stop working.
No: blocking a plugin blocks that plugin and the agents that depend on it, but associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins such as Plugin2.
No: Delete is available only for plugins and skills that were uploaded to your tenant. Plugin2 comes from the Microsoft 365 Store, so you can block it or limit its users instead.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. runs an internal remote MCP server named OrdersMCP with a public endpoint and API key authentication. The server must be governed by Agent 365 and then used by a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: Make sure that the Agent 365 service principal is provisioned, and install Agent 365 CLI version 1.1.165-preview or later.
Register OrdersMCP with the Agent 365 CLI register-external-mcp-server command, with the server URL, the APIKey authentication type and the tools.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Tools > Requests (preview), review the declared tools, and select Approve.
Consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions that OrdersMCP requires.
In Copilot Studio, open the agent, go to Tools, select MCP Server, and select OrdersMCP from the registry.
In Agents > Settings > Gateways, turn on the Microsoft Azure toggle.
In Agents > Tools > Registry, select Upload, and upload the OrdersMCP manifest.
explanation: Bring-your-own MCP servers follow a developer-to-admin flow: register with the Agent 365 CLI, admin approval on the Tools Requests tab, consent to Entra permissions, then use from a supported client such as Copilot Studio. Approved servers can take up to 30 minutes to appear in Copilot Studio.
rationale: Step 1: registration needs the Agent 365 CLI at the required version and the Agent 365 service principal in the tenant.
Step 2: the register-external-mcp-server command records the server URL, the APIKey authentication type and the tools, which creates the request.
Step 3: the registration appears on the Requests (preview) tab, where an admin reviews the declared tools and approves it.
Step 4: after approval, consent to the server's Entra permissions is required; only then is the server available to agent-building surfaces.
Step 5: in Copilot Studio, the approved server is picked from the registry under Tools > MCP Server.
Incorrect: the Gateways toggle connects Azure API Management so its registered servers are discovered. OrdersMCP is a standalone server registered with the CLI.
Incorrect: Upload in the Tools registry takes manifests for plugins and skills. MCP servers are registered through the CLI flow instead.

stem:
Lamna Healthcare has a plugin named ExpenseHelper that its developers uploaded to the tenant. Users must not be able to install any plugins from third-party publishers. Only the Finance group may use ExpenseHelper, and other agents and plugins must remain available to all users.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: In Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access, clear the option for external publishers.
In Agents > Tools > Plugins, open ExpenseHelper, and set Users to Specific users and groups: Finance.
Set User access to Specific users or groups, and select Finance.
Block ExpenseHelper in Agents > Tools > Plugins.
Delete every third-party plugin from the Tools registry.
explanation: Plugin availability has two levels: organization-level publisher categories in Agent and plugin access, and per-plugin user availability (All users, No users or Specific users and groups) on the plugin itself. Tenant-wide User access affects every agent and plugin.
rationale: Correct: clearing the external publishers category prevents users from installing third-party plugins, while Microsoft and organization plugins stay governed separately.
Correct: per-plugin availability with Specific users and groups limits ExpenseHelper to Finance without affecting other plugins.
Incorrect: User access limits all agents and plugins to Finance, which breaks the requirement that other agents remain available to all users. Use it for pilots.
Incorrect: blocking ExpenseHelper stops everyone, including Finance, from using it. Use Block when a plugin must be stopped organization-wide.
Incorrect: Delete applies only to plugins uploaded to the tenant, not to store plugins, and it would not stop future third-party installs. Use the publisher setting instead.

stem:
Refer to the case study. You need to choose where the ticketing team should build the agent that uses TicketingMCP.

Which surface should the ticketing team use?
choices: Microsoft Copilot Studio
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
A declarative agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
GitHub Copilot CLI
explanation: During the preview, approved bring-your-own MCP servers can be used from Copilot Studio, Visual Studio Code, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI. Foundry and Microsoft 365 declarative agents are not supported. Calls go through the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway, so Defender advanced hunting can track them.
rationale: Correct: Copilot Studio supports approved BYO MCP servers from the registry under Tools > MCP Server, and it is the low-code option that the requirements ask for.
Incorrect: Foundry agents are not a supported client surface for BYO MCP servers during the preview, so the agent could not use the approved TicketingMCP registration.
Incorrect: Microsoft 365 declarative agents are also listed as not supported for BYO MCP servers during the preview.
Incorrect: GitHub Copilot CLI is a supported client, but it is a developer command-line tool, not a low-code way to build and publish an agent for staff.
